verses.text: The elder, to my dear friend Gaius, whom I love in the truth:
Dear friend, I pray that everything is going well with you and that you’re healthy, just as your soul is doing well.
I was overjoyed when some believers came and testified about your faithfulness to the truth and how you keep living by it.
I have no greater joy than hearing that my children are living by the truth.
Dear friend, you’re faithful in what you do for the brothers and sisters, even though they’re strangers to you.
They told the church about your love. Please send them on their way in a manner worthy of God.
They went out for the sake of the Name, accepting no support from the nations.
So we should support people like them, so we can work together for the truth.
I wrote something to the church, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first, won’t welcome us.

So when I come, I’ll point out what he’s doing, spreading malicious nonsense about us. And he’s not satisfied with that: he refuses to welcome the believers and stops those who want to welcome them, even putting them out of the church.
Dear friend, don’t imitate what is evil, but what is good. Whoever does good belongs to God; whoever does evil hasn’t seen God.
Everyone speaks well of Demetrius, and so does the truth itself. We also speak well of him, and you know our testimony is true.
I have much to write to you, but I don’t want to do it with pen and ink.
I hope to see you soon, and we’ll talk face to face. Peace to you. The friends here send greetings. Greet the friends there by name.
